## Diagnosis — final consolidation

The archive now traces a clean frontier, and the trade-off is driven by two construction choices:

| construction | fmb | alpha | t(α) | Sharpe | cov |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (che + 3y CF) / 3y capex | 3.72 | 5.6% | 4.45 | **0.41** | .112 |
| (che + CF) / (capex + dlc) | 2.72 | 6.8% | 5.71 | 0.39 | .110 |
| (che + MA CF) / (MA capex + dlc) | 2.15 | **7.1%** | 5.65 | 0.38 | .112 |
| MAX(cash cover, flow cover) | 1.16 | 6.9% | 5.73 | 0.34 | .110 |
| (che + ib + dp) / (capex + dlc) | 2.03 | 5.9% | 5.23 | 0.30 | **.133** |
| coverage + utilization (SUMRANK) | 3.98 | 4.6% | 4.46 | 0.34 | .110 |
| 3-way conjunctive screen | **4.74** | 3.0% | 3.10 | 0.35 | .111 |

Two regularities: **multi-year cumulation raises the FMB slope**, while **adding maturing debt to commitments raises alpha** — and no signal has yet combined both, because the earlier attempt mixed a one-year debt stock with three-year capex sums (a unit error the critic flagged). Second, **pairing the coverage ratio with a second, operating-side channel raises the slope but costs alpha**, and the three-way conjunction shows the cost comes from including a leg with no standalone alpha (`capx/dp`, α=0.3%). So the final batch (i) builds the unit-consistent three-year cover of capex *and* maturing debt, (ii) isolates whether the accrual adjustment still earns its keep at that horizon, (iii) rescues the slope of the two highest-alpha constructions by pairing them with the utilization channel only, and (iv) tests the two-channel conjunction that drops the alpha-less leg.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Three-year cover of capex and maturing debt
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(dlc, 3))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Funding adequacy is best measured over a full investment cycle: cash on hand plus three years of cash generation against three years of capital spending and three years of short-term debt obligations, so that neither lumpy capex nor a single year's refinancing schedule distorts the assessment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the one combination the archive has never tested cleanly — three-year cumulation delivers the family's strongest slope and Sharpe (fmb 3.72, 0.41) while maturing debt delivers its strongest alpha (6.8–7.1%) — and it is dimensionally consistent because both denominator terms are three-year sums, repairing the unit error that made the earlier hybrid capex-dominated. If the two effects are additive rather than substitutes, this should be the archive's best joint-evidence signal.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Three-year unadjusted cover of capex and maturing debt
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(dlc, 3))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Over a three-year window, working-capital swings largely wash out, so cumulated cash earnings should measure fundable resources as well as the accrual-adjusted version while requiring less data history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The accrual adjustment was decisive at one-year horizons in the capex-only family (0.4% versus 4.1% alpha) but the same-period debt-denominator ablation showed it is now worth only about one point of alpha (5.9% versus 6.8%) at materially higher coverage, and its value over a three-year window is untested. Paired with Signal 1 this isolates the accrual adjustment's marginal contribution at the cycle horizon, which determines whether the recommended signal needs a prior-year balance-sheet reconstruction at all.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: High-coverage cover plus operating utilization
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(che, ADD(ib, dp)), ADD(capx, dlc)), SUB(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), MA(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The two-condition logic — commitments must be fundable and installed capital must be working harder than its own norm — should hold with the simplest available resource measure, giving a signal with both forms of evidence on the widest panel.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The utilization channel has lifted the slope of every coverage leg it has been paired with (fmb 3.98 with the accrual-adjusted leg, 2.65 with the gross-profit leg), and the unadjusted cash-earnings leg is the highest-alpha member of the family at the highest coverage (5.9%, t=5.23, cov 0.133), so this pairing targets joint strength without the data-history cost. Coupled with the two prior tests of this pairing it also identifies which numerator is the best partner for the operating channel.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Best single source cover plus utilization
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MAX(WINSOR(RATIO(che, ADD(capx, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ADD(capx, dlc)), 1)), SUB(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), MA(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Sufficiency of a single funding source identifies safe investors, and adding the operating-utilization condition supplies the cross-sectional discrimination that the sufficiency measure alone lacks.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The MAX construction produced the archive's joint-best alpha reliability (6.9%, t=5.73) but its weakest slope (fmb 1.16), precisely the profile that the utilization channel has repeatedly repaired, and the two legs share no variables. This is the most promising remaining route to a signal with alpha above 5% *and* a slope above 3, which is what the objective rewards.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Two-channel conjunctive screen
EXPRESSION: MIN(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, MA(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), 3)), ADD(MA(capx, 3), dlc)), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), MA(RATIO(sale, ADD(ppent, invt)), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm qualifies as a disciplined investor only if it clears both the financing hurdle and the utilization hurdle; requiring a third hurdle with no independent abnormal return simply adds noise to the screen.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The three-way conjunction produced the archive's best slope (fmb 4.74) but lost more than half the alpha, and the natural diagnosis is that the minimum is frequently set by the replacement-adjusted capex leg, which has zero standalone alpha — dropping it should retain most of the slope while restoring alpha. Because the additive version of the same two channels is already evaluated (fmb 3.98, alpha 4.6%), this cleanly identifies whether conjunction or averaging is the better aggregation for the final recommendation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: High-coverage trough cover of commitments
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_MIN(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), ADD(capx, dlc)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Resources should be measured by the cash earnings a firm can rely on — its weakest of the last three years — because commitments must be met even in a bad year; using unadjusted cash earnings keeps the measure available for a much wider set of firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Two independently validated improvements are combined here for the first time: the trough numerator raised alpha to 6.6% with a stronger slope than the smoothed leader, and dropping the working-capital reconstruction raised coverage from 0.110 to 0.133 at a cost of only one alpha point. Taking the minimum over three years of a simple, well-populated flow also makes the signal robust to single-year accrual distortions without needing the prior-year balance sheet, so it is the most deployable candidate if it retains the family's evidence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Three-year cover of capex and maturing debt---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A genuinely untested permutation within a heavily mined family with clear diagnostic purpose, but the stated "dimensional repair" is overstated since `dlc` is a balance-sheet stock and `TS_SUM(dlc,3)` only proxies three years of rollover under a strong assumption, while `che` remains a point-in-time stock against three-year flows.

---CRITIQUE Three-year unadjusted cover of capex and maturing debt---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The motivating claim is economically wrong — `TS_SUM(DELTA(WC,1),3)` telescopes to the three-year *level* change in working capital, which grows systematically with the firm rather than washing out, so the accrual adjustment is if anything more consequential at this horizon — and stripped of that rationale the proposal is a minor ablation of an existing archive ratio.

---CRITIQUE High-coverage cover plus operating utilization---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the third numerator swap in an already twice-evaluated SUMRANK pairing (accrual-adjusted leg fmb 3.98/alpha 4.6%, gross-profit leg fmb 2.65/alpha 3.8%), making it a cosmetic variant whose only differentiator is a ~2pp coverage gain rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Best single source cover plus utilization---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Same SUMRANK template as prior archive entries, but the pairing is properly diagnosed — a high-alpha/weak-slope sufficiency leg combined with an orthogonal slope-strengthening channel — so the test has a defensible ex ante rationale rather than being arbitrary recombination.

---CRITIQUE Two-channel conjunctive screen---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: A well-motivated ablation that isolates which leg of the three-way MIN destroys alpha and, jointly with the already-evaluated additive version, cleanly separates conjunctive from averaging aggregation — the most informative test in this batch despite operating inside a saturated family.

---CRITIQUE High-coverage trough cover of commitments---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Combining the trough numerator with the unadjusted cash-earnings simplification is a legitimate first-time pairing of two separately validated changes with a real coverage benefit, though it is a two-ingredient swap in an existing ratio and is mislabelled `novel` when it is plainly a ratio.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cover of fixed, working-capital and debt cash calls
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), ADD(ADD(TS_SUM(capx, 3), TS_SUM(dlc, 3)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 3))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Over an investment cycle a firm's cash calls are threefold — fixed capital spending, the cash permanently sunk into growing working capital, and short-term debt to be repaid — and resources should be measured against all three rather than netting the working-capital build out of earnings.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The critic's telescoping observation is exactly right and turns into a new economic claim rather than an ablation: the three-year working-capital change is a genuine, systematically growing investment outlay, so it belongs on the commitment side of the ledger where it competes with capex for the same cash, and DELTA(WC, 3) measures it directly at the same horizon as the other two terms. This is a substantively different accounting of investment from every archive signal — which treats working capital only as a deduction from cash generation — and the denominator remains dominated by the two strictly positive three-year sums, so the ordering stays stable.
REASONING_END
---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Self-funding surplus weighted by capital irreversibility
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(ppegt, at), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(ib, dp), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), ADD(capx, dlc)), at), 1))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Self-funding matters most where capital is irreversible: for a firm whose balance sheet is dominated by gross fixed assets, a funding shortfall forces distressed sales of assets that cannot be redeployed, whereas an asset-light firm can retrench cheaply, so the same surplus or deficit carries very different consequences.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is the theme's core interaction claim implemented without the defects of earlier attempts — the weighting variable (gross PP&E over assets) appears nowhere in the surplus measure, so nothing cancels algebraically as it did when commitment intensity multiplied a commitment-scaled ratio, and the weight is strictly non-negative and bounded in [0, 1], so the ordering is monotone in the surplus with no masked zero mass. It pairs the archive's best-slope funding measure (asset-scaled surplus, fmb 3.54, alpha 4.3%) with a real-options conditioning variable rather than a third numerator swap in an already twice-tested composite.
REASONING_END
